cards.front: Recall a key point about Plate Tectonics Theory
cards.back: Plate tectonics states the lithosphere is divided into large plates that move on the asthenosphere, driven by convection currents in the mantle

cards.front: Recall a key point about Plate Tectonics Theory
cards.back: Divergent boundaries: plates move apart (e.g. Mid-Atlantic Ridge), creating new oceanic crust

cards.front: Recall a key point about Plate Tectonics Theory
cards.back: Convergent boundaries: plates collide; oceanic-continental produces subduction zones and volcanoes; continental-continental produces fold mountains

cards.front: Recall a key point about Plate Tectonics Theory
cards.back: Transform boundaries: plates slide past each other (e.g. San Andreas Fault), causing earthquakes

cards.front: Recall a key point about Plate Tectonics Theory
cards.back: Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912, citing fossil, rock and coastline evidence, but the mechanism was unknown

cards.front: Recall a key point about Plate Tectonics Theory
cards.back: Seafloor spreading was confirmed by paleomagnetic striping in oceanic crust and age dating of ocean floor rocks
